text:
Jen Park: Quick proposal — introduce an 'elastic cushion' pool type for Dedicated. It acts as a small, always-available soft buffer that can absorb short tenant bursts without touching reserved quotas.
Priya Shah: can you sketch the main guarantees? latency/timeout behavior when cushion used?
Jen Park: idea: cushion = small pool (configurable per-account) that is pre-warmed. Guarantees: p95 latency same as reserved pool for <= cushion_size, p99 may degrade but within SLO. Preemption: cushion is preemptible after 30s if capacity pressure.
Sam Ortiz: what about billing? customers will expect predictable cost. If we let them "burn" cushion, do we charge from reserved quota or a separate burst bucket?
Jen Park: proposal: cushion consumption draws from a new "cushion credits" balance. Credits auto-replenish slowly (daily) based on their reserved commit size. Unused cushion credits do NOT roll over beyond 7 days in v1 to avoid long tail liabilities.
Luis Gomez: SRE note — preemption after 30s seems short. If a tenant gets preempted mid-inference it can cause failed requests. Need graceful drain + fallback routing.
Jen Park: Agreed. Spec includes KV cache checkpointing and immediate fallback to a cheaper model variant if preempted. Fallback route must keep request integrity for sync calls.
Priya Shah: launch criteria? seems risky to ship global. Recommend canary with 3 customers: 1 low-latency web app, 1 batch-heavy partner, 1 enterprise with SLA.
Sam Ortiz: +1 for canary. Also require observability: per-tenant cushion burn rate, preempt events, average extra latency, and cushion-credit balance trend.
Maia (devex): UX question — how will customers configure cushion? UI + API?
Jen Park: both. API endpoint: `POST /v1/dedicated/pools/:pool_id/cushion` with `{ "size": <gpu_units>, "credits_per_day": <units>, "preempt_window_s": 30 }`. UI will expose slider and warnings about preempt risk.
Sam Ortiz: please add server-side validation: max cushion <= 5% of reserved pool by default, and an opt-in higher cap for enterprise.
Jen Park: noted. Also adding a small CLI snippet for canary testing: ```sh
# create cushion for canary-tenant
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"size": 2, "credits_per_day": 10}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/pools/p-canary/cushion
```
Luis Gomez: autoscale interaction: if cushion gets drained often, autoscaler must consider cushion exhaustion as a signal to scale up earlier. Otherwise we'll just preempt a bunch and cause errors.
Jen Park: agree — autoscale rule: if cushion_burn_rate > threshold for N consecutive windows, raise target by +1 node immediately and extend cooldown to avoid oscillation. Adding to spec.
Priya Shah: scope negotiation: billing integration and 7-day non-rollover are product decisions. If finance insists on immediate pro-rated billing for cushion use, that adds backend tax. Suggest we ship v1 with credit model and a simple billing export CSV, then iterate.
Sam Ortiz: ops question — what's the rollback plan if cushion causes regressions?
Jen Park: revert flow: UI toggle per-customer to disable cushion, routing fallback to reserved-only path, and emergency global kill-switch in console. Canary must exercise kill-switch.
Maia (devex): docs: need clear error messages for when requests hit preemption: e.g., `INFERENCE_PREEMPTED -> try again or fallback enabled`. We'll add examples and guidance for handling idempotency.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: staging/cushion-feature -> QA tests -> canary deploy to p-canary cluster on 2134570000.
Jen Park: timeline proposal: spec PR this week, alpha in two weeks (internal), canary in 6 weeks, GA in 12 weeks if canary metrics passing.
Luis Gomez: add SLO gates: p99 < 250ms increase vs baseline for web-customer, <=1% increase in failed requests due to preemption for canary.
Priya Shah: agree to SLOs. Also add evaluation checklist: load profile, synthetic burst, KV cache hit-rate diff, billing export validation.
Sam Ortiz: putting action items in product board. I can own the observability panels. Priya — you want to own canary recruitment?
Priya Shah: I will take canary recruitment, Jen — can you open the spec PR and include the API contract?
Jen Park: on it. Will link PR and tracking ticket shortly. :thumbsup:
Maia (devex): I'll draft the shortstart doc and code examples for devs.
Jen Park: thanks all. We'll reconvene after spec PR reviews.
